subsystems.name: Transmitter and antenna
subsystems.role: produces a narrow, powerful beam that stays detectable across light-years.
parts: high-power amplifier (klystron, gyrotron or travelling-wave tube)

subsystems.name: Carrier and modulation
subsystems.role: chooses the wavelength and how information is imprinted on it.
parts: frequency choice in a quiet spectral band

subsystems.name: Message encoding
subsystems.role: turns meaning into something decodable without a shared language.
parts: prime-factor framing to signal a grid

subsystems.name: Target selection
subsystems.role: picks stars worth the cost of a decades-long wait.

subsystems.name: Pointing and tracking
subsystems.role: keeps the beam on a moving target for the whole transmission.

subsystems.name: Decision and risk framework
subsystems.role: settles who may transmit, to whom, and on what grounds.

buildSteps.title: Choose the target
buildSteps.detail: Select nearby Sun-like stars, preferring systems with known planets. Calculate how long the signal takes to arrive and how long a reply would take to return — a distant cluster can mean tens of thousands of years each way, which makes the exercise largely symbolic.

buildSteps.title: Choose the carrier
buildSteps.detail: Radio is cheaper per bit and passes through interstellar dust and gas; optical lasers give a much narrower beam but demand far more precise pointing. Pick a frequency in a quiet part of the spectrum, conventionally near the 1420 MHz hydrogen line that any radio astronomer would recognise.

buildSteps.title: Design the encoding
buildSteps.detail: Build the message in layers that assume nothing about the receiver's language: a counting sequence, then arithmetic, then physical constants and atomic numbers, then images. Frame the whole thing as a bit string whose length factors into two primes, so a receiver can guess to fold it into a rectangle.

buildSteps.title: Add redundancy and framing
buildSteps.detail: Repeat the message and include synchronisation headers so a receiver can find the frame start without being told where it is. Assume many bits will be lost to noise.

buildSteps.title: Secure the transmitter
buildSteps.detail: Book time on a large dish or build a dedicated beacon. Detectability scales with dish aperture and transmit power together, so a small dish with a big amplifier rarely competes with a big dish with a modest one.

buildSteps.title: Transmit
buildSteps.detail: Track the target across the sky and radiate repeatedly over a window while it is visible, logging frequency, power, beam direction and exact bit stream.

buildSteps.title: Archive and listen
buildSteps.detail: Publish the transmission record so future generations know what was sent and where, and keep the receiving programme running, because any reply arrives decades to millennia later.

prerequisites.tech: Large-aperture radio telescopes and high-power amplifiers
prerequisites.why: determines whether the signal is detectable at all at interstellar distances.
you need to know exactly where to point and whether the target has planets.
the same dishes verify a candidate band is quiet and would detect any reply.
primer-then-payload schemes have been proposed and used symbolically, but nobody knows whether they would actually be understood.
there is no binding mechanism to decide who speaks for humanity or how transmission risk is weighed.
a beacon only makes sense over timescales far longer than typical funding cycles.

pathway.milestone: one-off symbolic transmissions from large dishes, plus continued open debate
pathway.unlocks: practical experience with encoding, pointing and public reaction.

pathway.milestone: international consultation producing agreed risk-rating and decision procedures
pathway.unlocks: a legitimate basis for any deliberate, sustained transmission.

pathway.milestone: a purpose-built beacon with a documented, layered message and published target list
pathway.unlocks: a signal that is repeatable and verifiable rather than a gesture.

pathway.milestone: a listening programme matched to the transmission, capable of recognising a reply
pathway.unlocks: the only test of whether any of the message design actually worked.
